evidence: Skill procedure (quality-checks.md:14-15): verify sentence variety, contractions, occasional terse fragment; defect = uniform cadence, marketing gloss (seamless/robust/delve), perfectly parallel bullets, or voice change between instruction.md and notes. instruction.md reads as a team lead talking: opens 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (L1), states the stake plainly 'so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' (L1), uses first person throughout ('I often move several candidates together' L3; 'whether I am reading or halfway through a reply, never touch my draft or my cursor' L7), short terse sentences mixed with long ones ('A clear desktop workspace is what matters.' / 'We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' L11), and a personal request to self-test (L13). 7 contractions in instruction.md, 40 in hireops_rules.md. Grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamline|utilize|facilitate|furthermore|moreover|additionally and em/en dashes: zero hits in instruction.md, hireops_rules.md and integration.md. Notes keep the same 'we/I' requester voice with reasons rather than bare must-lists (Colderwater lesson 12 checked): 'We like to know where a card was when it was rejected, because reopening takes it back to exactly that stage' (rules L50-51); 'Several of us work the same board, so every card carries a version' (L78); 'When I move a card I want to see it move straight away' (L86); 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands' (L126); 'Some conversations run long, so...' (L150); 'Candidates are outside the company, so...' (L199); 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder' (L206). Modal density is low: rules.md has 0 must/shall, 1 should; instruction.md 2 must, 1 mustn't. Bullets are few (rules L70-74, L136-140, L164-166) and are natural role lists, not mirrored acceptance items. No voice break: instruction.md and hireops_rules.md share register ('turned down', 'we', 'I'). integration.md L1-14 is the template-controlled neutral technical note (frozen template integration.md); the task-added paragraphs L16-23 ('We copy /app as ordinary files when we deploy it, so please don't rely on symbolic links...') match the requester voice. Minor, non-blocking observations: (a) instruction.md L15 is a parallel run-on runtime list ('It must start with..., listen on..., expose..., serve..., and keep...') and rules L22-24/L79 cite HTTP codes 401/403/404/409; these are the required runtime contract (row 4) phrased in plain sentences and do not make the prose robotic. (b) Definitional passages (Unread L157-160, Seen L170-172, Undo L99-104) are dense but still in first person with reasons. (c) rules.md L99 and L187 are unwrapped long lines unlike the surrounding ~100-col wrapping, a sign of later insertion; this is formatting hygiene (row 3 territory), not voice. Counterexample search: tried to find LLM tells (triads of adjectives, 'not just X but Y', hedged summaries, closing pleasantries, headings like 'Overview/Requirements') and a voice shift between files; none found. A broken or conforming app does not bear on this text-only row.
